title: Anthropic Launches Claude Duet, a Proactive Agent Challenging Gemini on Android
excerpt: Anthropic opened a research preview of Claude Duet on October 21, a standalone Android, iPhone and web app that messages users first, works in the background and asks before sending, paying or deleting anything.
body:
• Anthropic launched Claude Duet, a proactive work agent, as a research preview on Android, iPhone and the web on October 21.
  • Access is by waitlist for U.S. Claude Pro and Max subscribers only; it is not yet available on Team or Enterprise plans.
  • Duet runs on Claude Opus 5.5, connects to more than 6,000 apps and plugins, and sends a short morning brief across connected apps.
  • It asks for approval before sending a message, making a payment, signing a document or deleting anything, and shares the plan's existing usage limits.

Anthropic has entered the personal-agent race with Claude Duet, a standalone app that the company describes as a proactive agent rather than a chatbot that waits for prompts. Announced on October 21, Duet is available as a research preview on Android, iPhone and the web, putting Anthropic in direct competition with Google's Gemini agent features, Meta Muse, Microsoft Autopilot and OpenAI Dots, according to reporting by Thurrott and Engadget.

Unlike the main Claude app, Duet is designed to come to the user first. Each morning it sends a short brief on the most important items across connected apps, then checks those accounts every few hours during the day and messages the user only when something needs attention, Anthropic says.

Context

Anthropic says it built Duet for professionals and small-business owners with more on their plates than they can track. The product is built around Claude Opus 5.5 and carries over a user's memory, skills and connected apps from a regular Claude account, so a quick reply and a weeklong project can start in the same ongoing thread, by typing or voice.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=_eY1lyoYKqE

Users can hand Duet tasks ranging from scheduling meetings to building dashboards with dozens of tools, creating financial or sales forecasts, prototyping and building web apps, the company says. Examples it lists include finding missed Gmail and Slack messages, checking QuickBooks or Stripe for unpaid invoices and drafting reminders, preparing payroll in Gusto, and drafting job postings for LinkedIn. Duet can use more than 6,000 connectors and plugins in the Claude Marketplace, according to Anthropic.

Duet runs on its own virtual machine with its own browser, so work continues in the background without a phone or laptop needing to stay on. The user receives a notification when a task is complete or needs review.

Impact and Analysis

The launch matters because every major AI lab is now converging on the same product idea: an agent that monitors connected tools and acts, within limits, on the user's behalf. Thurrott noted that Duet is specifically positioned for work, not everyday personal tasks, and that Anthropic appears to have arrived after its rivals in this category. Engadget made a similar point, calling Duet Anthropic's answer to Meta Muse and OpenAI Dots.

Anthropic is emphasizing approval and safety as the differentiator. Duet reads, drafts and prepares work on its own, but before it sends a message, makes a payment, signs a document or deletes anything, it shows the user what it is about to do and waits for approval, the company says. A few actions are off limits even with approval, including trading securities or moving money between accounts. Anthropic also says Duet never directly sees passwords or sign-in tokens, and that a new classifier and system prompt guard against leaking sensitive information, with health or personal-finance information shared only when the user explicitly instructs it.

There is a cost in usage. Duet is included in Pro and Max plans at no additional charge for the preview, but its background checks and larger tasks count toward the same usage limits as the rest of Claude, which Anthropic warns could cause users to reach those limits sooner than with chat alone.

What's Next

Access is narrow for now. Anthropic is starting with Pro and Max users in the United States through a waitlist, with invitations sent in waves, and Duet is not yet available on Team or Enterprise plans, though the company says it plans to expand availability. Anthropic is candid that this is an early version: it says Duet may still misread a thread, misjudge urgency or miss something that arrives between checks, and that personal errands such as booking tickets are not yet as strong as its work functions.

For Android users, the test will be whether a work-focused, third-party agent can compete with Gemini's built-in position on the platform. Duet's pitch is judgment and breadth across thousands of connected apps rather than native integration. Whether professionals trust an agent with that much of their working life, and whether the usage limits hold up under always-on checking, will decide if the preview becomes a durable product.
